newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sells three airports for A$3.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Australia sells three airports for A$3.3 bln.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday that it had sold long-term leases to three capital city airports for A$3.3 billion (US$2.57 billion).

Melbourne airport was awarded to Australian Pacific Airports Corp (APAC), a consortium led by British airports operator BAA Plc and Australian funds manager Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) for A$1.307 billion, Finance Minister John Fahey told reporters.
The lease for Brisbane airport was awarded to a group headed by Dutch government-owned Amsterdam Airport Schiphol and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia Ltd for A$1.387 billion.

Perth was sold for A$643 million to Airstralia Development Group Pty Ltd, a consortium that includes Airport Group Holdings International (a subsidiary of Lockheed Martin Corp and Soros Capital), an infrastructure subsidiary of HRL Morrison & Co and Hastings Fund Management.
The three airport sales are the first phase of the privatisation of more than 20 government airports in capital cities and regional centres around the country.
The original contracts are for 50-year leases, with an option of a further 49 years.
